issues.legal_issue: The requisition statute applied to territory incorporated into a state even though that territory previously had no corresponding requisition law.
material_facts: The territory was made part of the state and its Hooghly district under the merger legislation.
The merger legislation extended laws in force in the state generally to the territory, and later assimilation legislation extended state laws on matters in the State List.
The requisition statute concerned acquisition and requisitioning of property, and also addressed compensation for acquired or requisitioned property.
There was no corresponding requisition law in force in the territory before its incorporation.
The requisition orders were challenged on the grounds that the statute had not been extended to the territory and that the absence of a corresponding law prevented its application.
issues.conclusion: The requisition statute applied to the territory; the absence of a corresponding local law did not prevent its extension, and conflicting privileges or immunities ceased to operate.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Chandernagore (Merger) Act, 1954 made the territory part of West Bengal, and section 17 extended laws in force in West Bengal generally to it. The court construed “generally” as referring to territory, not the duration for which a law operated. The West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 related to acquisition and requisitioning of property under List II, Entry 36, and to compensation under List III, Entry 42. Sections 3 and 4 of the Chandernagore (Assimilation of Laws) Act, 1955 extended laws on List II matters and repealed corresponding laws; section 4 did not limit section 3 where no corresponding law existed. Section 3 of the Assimilation Act, together with section 17 of the Merger Act and the relevant statutory definitions, extended the Act insofar as it concerned List III matters. No earlier case is relied on in the supplied judgment.

predicates.challenge_to_requisition_order: A person challenged an order made under a law authorizing requisition of property.
predicates.territory_integrated_into_state: The territory where the property was situated became part of the state under an integration measure.
predicates.state_law_applied_generally_to_state_ter: The relevant extension measure applied state laws generally across the state's territory, rather than only for a specified duration.
predicates.law_concerned_property_requisition_or_ac: The law governed the requisition or acquisition of property, including related compensation matters.

issues.definition: When an order under a property-requisition law is challenged for territory integrated into a state, and the law was generally applicable to the state and concerned property requisition or acquisition, the rule means that the requisition law applies in the integrated territory.

issues.legal_issue: An officer empowered to requisition land within a district may act in territory that later becomes part of that district, and a duly specially appointed officer may exercise the relevant collector's functions.
material_facts: A 1948 notification authorized the district Collector to requisition land within the local limits of the Collector's jurisdiction.
When that notification was issued, the territory containing the land was not part of the district; it was later incorporated into the district.
The requisition orders were made after the territory had become part of the district.
A 1959 notification specially appointed the Additional District Magistrate to perform the functions of a Collector under the requisition statute.
The challenged orders purported to be made by the district Collector; the court also considered the authority of the Additional District Magistrate if that officer had issued them.
issues.conclusion: The district Collector was authorized to requisition land in the territory after it became part of the district; the specially appointed Additional District Magistrate was also authorized to act as a Collector.
issues.legal_principle: The 1948 notification authorizing a Collector to requisition land within the local limits of the Collector's jurisdiction refers to the district limits as they exist when the power is exercised. Under the requisition statute's definition of “Collector,” an officer specially appointed by the state government to perform a Collector's functions is included; the 1959 notification amounted to such a special appointment. No earlier case is relied on in the supplied judgment.

predicates.challenge_to_requisition_order: A person challenged an order made to requisition land.
predicates.land_within_district_when_power_exercise: The land was within the district's boundaries when the requisition power was exercised, including because the territory had since become part of the district.
predicates.district_collector_issued_order: The district Collector issued the requisition order under an authorization covering land within the Collector's jurisdiction.
predicates.officer_specially_appointed_as_collector: An officer specially appointed by the state government to perform a Collector's functions issued the requisition order.

issues.definition: For a challenged requisition order, if the land was within the district when the power was exercised, the rule means the officer was authorized when the order was issued either by the district Collector or by an officer specially appointed to perform a Collector's functions.

issues.legal_issue: The requisition statute was not unconstitutional on the ground that it violated the constitutional right to property, subject to the permitted restrictions.
material_facts: The constitutional validity of the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 was questioned under Article 19(1)(f) read with Article 19(5) of the Constitution.
The Supreme Court referred the question to a Constitution Bench, which answered it in the negative.
issues.conclusion: The Act was not ultra vires the Constitution on the ground raised under Article 19(1)(f) read with Article 19(5).
issues.legal_principle: The Constitution Bench answered in the negative the question whether the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 was ultra vires Article 19(1)(f) read with Article 19(5). The supplied judgment gives no further reasoning on this issue and relies on no earlier case.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_property_req: A party challenged the constitutional validity of a law authorizing requisition of property.
predicates.challenge_based_on_property_right_and_pe: The constitutional challenge relied on the constitutional property right and its permitted restrictions.

issues.definition: When a property-requisition law is challenged on the basis of the property right and its permitted restrictions, the rule means that the law is not unconstitutional on that ground.
